approved_premise.override_reason: For the first Episode, establish the protagonist's cartographer role, mentor relationship, world navigation logic, and the first Main Saga anomaly. The Luna-selected fisher premise remains a strong later world-side candidate but gives a 12-year-old apprentice too much community route-safety responsibility too early.

premise.title: The Angle That Wouldn't Match
premise.logline: A routine beacon calibration turns into Deniz's first real test of whether patient observation can outweigh a mentor's doubt.
premise.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor conducting supervised but semi-independent beacon calibration checks.
premise.immediate_objective: Confirm whether a magnetic-stone beacon reading at Beacon Ridge is a genuine anomaly or an instrument error before the calibration window closes.
premise.inciting_event: While logging a routine reading, Deniz notices the beacon's angle has drifted further than tide tables allow, but the harbor's shipping logs show no confirming delays or complaints that would prove the drift is real.
premise.central_problem: Deniz has only a single suspicious reading and a narrow window before the tide changes and the anomaly becomes unmeasurable again, with no corroborating evidence yet and a mentor likely to dismiss a lone data point.
premise.wonder_or_discovery: A pattern emerges suggesting the drift is tied to tidal extremes rather than random error, hinting at something systematic in the old navigation network.
premise.stakes: If dismissed as a measurement mistake, a real anomaly worth investigating could go unrecorded for another season; if reported too early on thin evidence, Deniz risks being seen as overconfident and losing supervised field privileges.
constraints: Limited daylight and tide window at Beacon Ridge
Only supervised access to the beacon instruments
Mentor evaluates methodology, not just conclusions
premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: Deniz must decide whether to report the single unusual reading now, risking dismissal for insufficient evidence, or spend the remaining tide window trying to capture a second corroborating reading, risking losing the anomaly's window entirely if it doesn't recur.
premise.mystery_or_forward_question: Is this drift an isolated fluke, or the first visible sign of a larger disagreement between the old markers and the official charts?
premise.local_payoff: Deniz secures at least a provisional, logged acknowledgment of the anomaly, changing how the mentor treats future field reports.
persistent_outcomes_possible: Mentor's assessment of Deniz's methodology shifts (skeptical, cautious-respect, or dismissive)
A dated logbook entry becomes a reusable reference item
A rumor begins circulating among harbor navigators about 'the ridge beacon problem'
world_specific_elements: harbor shipping logs as corroborating evidence

dimensions.name: PREMISE_MATURITY
dimensions.description: Core story problem should feel substantively suitable for a 12-year-old, not like preschool play dressed in harder vocabulary.

dimensions.name: NARRATIVE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support layered goals, changing information, reversals, and multi-step progression while remaining readable.

dimensions.name: CONCEPTUAL_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Allow systems, evidence, competing explanations, responsibility, trust, and consequences without requiring adult-only abstraction.

dimensions.name: CAUSAL_DEPTH
dimensions.description: Important outcomes should follow from multiple linked causes rather than one-step problem-solution patterns.

dimensions.name: INFERENCE_DEMAND
dimensions.description: Reader should sometimes connect clues, motives, patterns, or consequences without every relationship being stated directly.

dimensions.name: AGENCY_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Character should face meaningful options, trade-offs, strategy, or uncertainty; choices must not be predetermined.

dimensions.name: STAKES_CONSEQUENCE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Actions should matter to reputation, relationships, access, goals, safety, or world state without requiring graphic danger.

dimensions.name: SOCIAL_RELATIONSHIP_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support trust, disagreement, rivalry, mentorship, competing interests, and mixed motives without adult melodrama.

dimensions.name: PREDICTABILITY_CHALLENGE
dimensions.description: Avoid obvious one-beat resolutions; allow wrong hypotheses, reversals, incomplete information, and earned payoff.

dimensions.name: WONDER_DISCOVERY
dimensions.description: Adventure-oriented episodes should offer places, systems, discoveries, mysteries, or experiences larger than ordinary daily-life simulation.

dimensions.name: LANGUAGE_READABILITY
dimensions.description: Use clear, natural language suitable for an independent 12-year-old reader. Story maturity must not depend on jargon.

required_story_capabilities: Meaningful protagonist role in the world
At least one non-trivial objective or unresolved question
Meaningful discovery or change in understanding
A real choice, strategic constraint, or consequential action
Persistent consequence or reusable world-state value
Adventure-oriented modes should include wonder, exploration, mystery, or extraordinary experience
reject_signals: Core premise is primarily pretend-play with toys, chores, or ordinary-room simulation unless explicitly requested
Difficult vocabulary is doing the work of making an otherwise young-child premise appear older
Problem resolves through one obvious attempt with no meaningful complication
Character mostly observes while adults or the world solve the important problem
Episode can be summarized as collect clue A, clue B, clue C with no reasoning change
Stakes are cosmetic and no persistent consequence can result
Mystery is solved before the character earns the relevant evidence
World can be swapped for any generic setting without changing the premise materially
language_rules: Technical terms are allowed when they serve the world or reasoning and can be understood in context
Do not infantilize dialogue or narration
Do not use vocabulary difficulty as a substitute for premise maturity
Keep exposition bounded and reveal information through action, observation, dialogue, or consequence where practical
safety_rules: Adventure tension is allowed without requiring graphic violence
Fear, danger, loss, rivalry, and uncertainty may be present when developmentally appropriate
Do not assume maturity requires darker or more violent content
Do not force romance, grief, betrayal, or trauma merely to make a story feel older
calibration_notes: A strong age-12 premise may involve systems failing, competing hypotheses, expedition planning, social disagreement, hidden history, evidence testing, or strategic risk.
A simple premise may still pass when deliberately selected for a calm/intimate mode, but should not be used as the default adventure ceiling.
Evaluate premise, narrative, conceptual, interest, and language maturity independently.

character.name: Deniz
character.origin_summary: Deniz grew up in Meridian Harbor apprenticing under a demanding mapmaker, driven to prove that patient observation can reveal what official charts miss.
character.current_role: apprentice cartographer under supervised but increasingly independent fieldwork

identity_anchors.statement: Deniz believes careful observation matters more than authority or bravado.
Deniz wants recognition earned through proof, not granted by rank.

core_drives.drive: Prove that rigorous observation reveals truths official maps miss.
Earn the right to chart beyond the home strait.

internal_tensions.side_b: pull toward reckless pursuit of a personally meaningful mystery
internal_tensions.description: Deniz's discipline is tested whenever a discovery brushes close to personal stakes.

immediate_desires: earn the right to chart beyond the home strait
find hard evidence others cannot dismiss
immediate_avoidances: being dismissed as a reckless or overconfident child surveyor

world.era: age of sail with precision mechanical navigation
world.habitat: a vast island chain divided by deep channels, storm belts and partially mapped outer seas
world.technology_level: sailing ships, mechanical clocks, optical instruments, printing presses and hand-built navigation devices
world.magic_level: rare, rule-bound geophysical phenomena associated with tides, magnetic stone and ancient infrastructure; no arbitrary spellcasting
world.summary: The Shattered Meridian is an archipelago civilization whose survival depends on maps. Most inner routes are well known, but outer charts disagree, old observatories stand on remote islands, drowned roads appear at extreme tides, and some navigation markers predate every living culture. The world rewards exploration, evidence and careful inference rather than effortless magic.
social_context: cartographers and navigators hold respected public roles
island councils depend on reliable sea routes
young apprentices may take meaningful expedition roles within established safety rules
merchant captains, fishers and scholars often disagree about what counts as trustworthy evidence
old folklore sometimes preserves real geographic information in distorted form
known_pressures: several navigation beacons no longer agree with official charts
outer-island routes are becoming economically important
storm season will eventually restrict long voyages
different groups have reasons to prefer different versions of the map
known_world_facts: Meridian Harbor is Deniz's home port and training base.
Beacon Ridge is part of the known inner navigation network.
The Drowned Causeway is known to appear only during rare low tides.
The Outer Mist Line marks the edge of reliable official charts.
An abandoned tide observatory exists on a distant mapped island.
Several beacon readings have recently become difficult to reconcile with official charts, but no accepted explanation exists yet.

main_saga_public.title: The Uncharted Disagreement
main_saga_public.goal: Discover why the Shattered Meridian's ancient navigation infrastructure and living tides no longer agree with official charts.
main_saga_public.stakes: Outer routes vital to island trade may become unsafe or unusable if the true cause of the discrepancies goes unaddressed.
main_saga_public.central_mystery: Something in the deep channels or the ancient beacon-markers is behaving in ways no known chart-making era can explain.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: Deniz notices a beacon reading that disagrees with the official chart by a margin too large for instrument error.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: Deniz has one documented anomaly and a working hypothesis that it is not simple mistake.
consequence_options: The friend becomes curious and offers to help verify.

active_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's practical-minded friend may want to pursue independent proof through experiments rather than surveying, creating friendly rivalry.
active_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Provides low-stakes roleplay and callback material outside the Main Saga.

creation_constraints: New entities must fit low-magic, rule-bound tidal/magnetic world logic.
New NPCs should have plausible reasons to intersect Deniz's apprentice life.
Do not contradict established hidden truths.

architect_raw_payload.title: The Angle That Wouldn't Match
architect_raw_payload.story_promise: Deniz tests a suspicious beacon reading against tide tables and a shrinking window, then must choose between reporting now and gambling on stronger evidence, with any record and mentor response earned by the outcome.
architect_raw_payload.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor conducting supervised but semi-independent beacon calibration checks.
architect_raw_payload.immediate_objective: Decide whether the Beacon Ridge magnetic-stone reading is a genuine anomaly or instrument error before the tide window closes.
architect_raw_payload.central_question: Can patient, well-documented observation outweigh a mentor's doubt about a single odd reading?
architect_raw_payload.stakes: A real anomaly may go unrecorded, or premature reporting may cost Deniz credibility and supervised field privileges.
constraints: Limited daylight and tide window at Beacon Ridge
Only supervised access to the beacon instruments
Mentor evaluates methodology, not just conclusions
Harbor shipping logs are records-only and show no corroborating complaints
architect_raw_payload.opening_hook: Deniz logs a routine reading and finds the beacon angle has drifted further than the tide table allows, just as the water begins to turn.

logistics_plan.time_window: About 90 minutes of usable light, with the measurable tide state shrinking toward slack and reversal; one fresh-setup retest costs roughly 25-30 minutes.
movement_constraints: All action stays on Beacon Ridge; no travel to Meridian Harbor.
Harbor shipping logs and tide tables are already in Deniz's field folder as copied records.
The mentor is on the ridge supervising and controls instrument access.
logistics_plan.feasibility_rationale: Every action is a short walk between the beacon, the sighting station and the mentor's post, so the whole sequence fits inside the window without harbor travel.

beats.character_action: Deniz takes a routine sighting and compares it with the tide table.
beats.external_event: The tide begins turning toward slack.
beats.new_information: The angle is off by more than the table allows.
beats.escalation_delta: A closing window starts the clock.
beats.state_change: Deniz holds one suspicious, unverified reading.
beats.payoff_contribution: Creates the uncertainty to be resolved.

beats.purpose: Show constraints and the mentor's standards.
beats.character_action: Deniz reviews the copied harbor shipping logs and mentions the drift cautiously to the mentor.
beats.external_event: The mentor says one reading is not a finding and demands method.
beats.new_information: The logs show no delays or complaints; the mentor will judge procedure.
beats.escalation_delta: Doubt and a lack of corroboration constrain what counts as proof.
beats.state_change: Deniz must earn credibility through method.
beats.payoff_contribution: Sets what any acknowledgment would require.

beats.character_action: Deniz checks level, sighting alignment and the previous log's reference marks.
beats.external_event: Wind gusts disturb the sighting station once.
beats.new_information: The setup looks sound, but the wind leaves a small doubt about the mount.
beats.escalation_delta: Simple error is less likely but not excluded.
beats.state_change: The error explanation weakens without collapsing.

beats.purpose: Test whether the drift varies with tide.
beats.character_action: Deniz takes timed repeat readings as the tide moves and records each against the table.
beats.external_event: The water level drops steadily toward slack.
beats.new_information: The offset shrinks as the tide state changes, in three timed readings.
beats.escalation_delta: The problem shifts from whether the reading is odd to whether it varies.
beats.state_change: A tide correlation becomes a bounded, within-session inference.
beats.payoff_contribution: Provides the wonder and the pattern.

beats.character_action: Deniz shows the readings; the mentor points out all were taken from one setup.
beats.external_event: The mentor notes the mount may have shifted or settled across the hour.
beats.new_information: Setup-dependence could mimic a tide pattern.
beats.escalation_delta: The evidence is challenged on method, not just size.
beats.state_change: The correlation stays plausible but contested.

beats.purpose: Reinterpret the drift as a possible tide-linked pattern rather than random fluke.
beats.character_action: Deniz lines up the timed offsets against the tide table and the reference marks.
beats.external_event: The final timed reading fits the trend before the tide nears slack.
beats.new_information: Within this session, offset and tide state moved together.
beats.escalation_delta: The easy dismissal now conflicts with observed data, yet remains possible.
beats.state_change: Deniz's belief moves from fluke to a possible, unproven pattern.

beats.character_action: Deniz weighs presenting the current record against using remaining time on a fresh-setup retest.
beats.external_event: The mentor prepares to close the session as the window shrinks.
beats.new_information: Reporting now uses the time; a retest may strengthen or weaken the case but may leave no time to write it up.
beats.escalation_delta: Time and credibility now trade directly against evidence.
beats.state_change: Deniz must commit to a path.

beats.purpose: Dramatize the chosen branch using earlier evidence and skill.
beats.character_action: Deniz executes the chosen branch: presents a methodical case, or re-sets and re-measures under time pressure.
beats.external_event: The tide nears slack and the mentor scrutinizes the method.
beats.new_information: Either the mentor accepts, qualifies or rejects the presentation, or the fresh readings strengthen, weaken or contradict the pattern.
beats.escalation_delta: The last minutes decide whether evidence and record both arrive.
beats.state_change: The outcome of the branch becomes known but not guaranteed to be recorded.

beats.purpose: Close the local uncertainty according to what was earned.
beats.character_action: Deniz records what the branch produced and accepts the mentor's response.
beats.external_event: The session closes with the mentor's verdict.
beats.new_information: A log exists only if a legible entry was produced and reviewed before closure.
beats.state_change: Branch-conditional: a durable log, mentor acknowledgment, relationship or access shift and milestone eligibility exist only if the entry was completed and reviewed. Otherwise Deniz has stronger evidence with no completed log, contradicting evidence with a partial note, or an unreviewed result.
beats.payoff_contribution: Deniz knows more about the reading than at the start, with consequences matching the choice.

beats.purpose: Open the forward question without erasing the payoff.
beats.character_action: Deniz looks at the beacon and notes what remains untested.
beats.external_event: The tide slackens and the offset can no longer be measured.
beats.new_information: Recurrence, cause and other beacons are untested.

escalation_ladder: The reading turns out to disagree with the tide table.
The harbor logs offer no corroboration, and the mentor demands method.
The mount and wind cast doubt on the setup.
The mentor raises setup-dependence as an alternative explanation.
The shrinking window forces a trade-off between reporting and evidence.

reversal.prior_belief: The drift is probably a one-off reading or instrument error.

evidence.claim: The setup checks found no obvious fault, though wind disturbed the station once.
Timed readings showed the offset shrinking as the tide state changed.
Within this session the offset and tide state moved together.
The mount may have settled and mimicked a tide pattern.

reversal.reinterpretation: The drift may be a tide-linked pattern rather than random error, but that remains contested.
reversal.inference_ceiling: Only a within-session correlation from one setup; no proof of recurrence, cause, other beacons or a wider Saga mechanism.
reversal.unresolved_after_reversal: Whether setup-dependence explains the pattern remains unresolved until a fresh-setup retest, if chosen; recurrence, cause and other beacons are also unknown.

decision_point.pressure: Report now on a contested record, or spend the shrinking window on a fresh-setup retest that may fail to leave time for a write-up.

branches.option: Report the current readings and method to the mentor immediately.
branches.immediate_action: Deniz presents the timed readings, the checks and the open setup objection, and requests a provisional entry.
branches.evidence_state_after_choice: Evidence stays single-setup with the setup-dependence objection open.
branches.cost_or_risk: The mentor may judge it overconfident, reject the methodology and decline any entry, and the tide window is lost for retesting.
branches.relationship_or_access_effect: May yield a cautious hearing or a rejection; either can shift the mentor's view and Deniz's supervised access.
branches.climax_requirement: Dramatize Deniz presenting honestly, naming the limits, and answering the mentor's challenge using b3 to b5.
branches.local_payoff_if_earned: Only if the mentor accepts the case, a provisional dated entry may be logged and reviewed. Otherwise Deniz gets pointed critique with no entry.

branches.option: Re-set the instrument from scratch and re-measure before slack.
branches.immediate_action: Deniz rebuilds the sighting setup, re-levels and takes fresh readings with the mentor watching.
branches.evidence_state_after_choice: New readings may confirm, weaken or contradict the pattern; setup-dependence is tested.
branches.cost_or_risk: Consumes reporting time; the result may be ambiguous, and no entry may be written or reviewed before closure.
branches.relationship_or_access_effect: Rigor may earn respect, or seem to delay; access effects depend on a reviewed result.
branches.climax_requirement: Dramatize a careful, time-pressed re-measurement and honest reading of the result against the earlier timed data.
branches.local_payoff_if_earned: Evidence earned is stronger, weaker or contradictory. Logging and acknowledgment are a second condition that may fail if time runs out; no record is guaranteed.

decision_point.what_is_unknown: Whether the pattern survives a fresh setup, and whether the mentor accepts either presentation.

architect_raw_payload.climax: Under the closing tide, Deniz uses the timed readings, setup checks and the mentor's objection to either defend a limited claim or test it with a fresh setup, then must act on the result before the window ends.
architect_raw_payload.local_payoff: Deniz resolves what can be resolved: whether the reading held up under scrutiny within this session, with consequences depending on the branch. A completed log, mentor acknowledgment, relationship or access shift and milestone eligibility exist only if the branch produced a legible entry that the mentor reviewed before closure.
architect_raw_payload.forward_hook: If the drift is real, is it isolated to this beacon or a sign of a wider disagreement between old markers and official charts?

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: A dated logbook entry usable as a reference.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if a legible entry was written and reviewed before closure.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Mentor's assessment of Deniz's methodology shifts.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if the mentor's response is dramatized in the delivered story.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Result of the retest or the mentor's critique.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if the readings or critique are shown on the page.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Harbor navigators begin talking about the ridge beacon problem.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Only if the story shows information leaving the ridge.

completion_evidence: A dated entry documents the anomaly.
The mentor reviewed the entry before closure.
The entry states its limits, including single-setup evidence unless retested.
Deniz holds a working hypothesis that it is not simple mistake.

anti_repetition_signature.core_problem_shape: Fragile evidence against a closing window and a skeptical reviewer
anti_repetition_signature.primary_activity: Timed instrument readings and methodological argument
anti_repetition_signature.main_location_pattern: Single site: Beacon Ridge, with the harbor as records only
anti_repetition_signature.distinct_from_recent_episodes_because: No recent episodes exist; the tension is in method, not travel or combat.

writer_rules: Keep all scenes on Beacon Ridge; Meridian Harbor appears only through copied records.
Do not guarantee a log, acknowledgment, relationship shift, access shift or milestone; make them depend on the chosen branch.
Do not precommit which branch Deniz picks; dramatize both options.
Do not claim recurrence, cause, other beacons or a wider Saga mechanism.
Keep the setup-dependence objection open until a chosen retest addresses it.
Do not add locked locations or new facts that contradict the spine.
Use clear language suited to a 12-year-old and keep to 1600-2500 words.

contract_error.message: Episode Spine targeting Main Saga milestone needs Main Saga episode role
